cells.tense: You're building the thing in front of you, and you're in the room with the people it touches while you build it.
cells.ask: offer someone a look at how you're working — inquiry you actually trust — and let their engagement refine you without tightening you
cells.core:
You can move something real into place without going cold, and the people around you can feel that you're still here while you do it. The work gets done and the relationships hold. Nothing is being sacrificed for the other. They're feeding each other — the building gives you something to share, and the sharing keeps the building honest about what it's for.

What you're free to feed next is the quieter half of this: time alone with the work isn't distance from anyone, and getting the details right can be something you do calmly instead of something you do because you're afraid of getting them wrong. Let someone see the method, not just the result. That's the part of this you haven't shown yet, and it's the part that would make the connection real instead of just steady.
cells.sheetLine: You build steadily and stay in contact while you build.
cells.verb: forcing structural change into reality, slow but unstoppable
cells.place: in the part of your life where you feel with people and stay aligned with them

cells.tense: You're living a few steps ahead again — bracing for how this needs to look once it's done, pushing the shape into place before anyone's ready for it.
cells.ask: teach one person the meaning behind what you're building, and let their version of it change how you say it
cells.core:
You want the people near you to already be where the finished thing puts them, so you keep steering them there. The push is coming from caring — you can see what it could be and you want them inside it now. But a structure forced faster than the people in it can hold doesn't connect anyone; it just leaves you alone with the blueprint, and the blueprint isn't company.

What's underneath is real, and it doesn't need to be driven that hard. Say what this thing means to you, tell it to one person, and let them take it in their own way. Belonging that has to be arranged stops being belonging. The transmission works better when it's offered and not installed.
cells.sheetLine: You're forcing the shape on people faster than they can take it in.
cells.verb: forcing structural change into reality, slow but unstoppable

cells.tense: You stopped putting your weight behind anything a while back, and you're still standing at that same spot, near people but not building with them.
cells.ask: take one clear position with someone this week — say where you stand and mean it
cells.core:
You have a real capacity to move things into place and keep them there, and the people around you can feel when that's missing — nothing quite holds, nothing quite lands, and the warmth you offer doesn't get a structure to land in. The shift is small, not a rebuild: pick one thing, one person, and put a decision behind it. The connection comes back through the acting, not before it.

Don't try to feel your way into alignment first — that's not where this starts for you. Say the clear thing, draw the line, let someone see you take a position. Being with people gets easier once you're actually standing somewhere. The stance is what they've been waiting for, and it's the thing that makes the care visible.
cells.sheetLine: You've gone quiet on the taking of positions, and connection went with it.

cells.tense: You're already holding things together for the people around you, and you're telling yourself it's just how things are.
cells.ask: notice one thing you keep going out of genuine care, and let that be your reason for it — then follow it
cells.core:
The steadiness is running — you're the one who keeps showing up, who stays with it, who doesn't let things fall apart for the people counting on you. It works, and it's not small. People rest on it. That's exactly why it's easy to let it stand in for something you'd have to admit you chose, and to keep describing it as just what's needed.

What's feeding it is simpler than a plan: movement from what you actually feel. Not the resolve you built around the feeling — the feeling itself. Tend one thing because it matters to you, and let that be the whole reason. The rest will follow it, and you'll be able to say it's yours.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding it all steady. You haven't said that you chose to.
